items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to establishing the New York state clean energy tech production program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1225

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public service law, in relation
to establishing the New York state clean energy tech production
program

 PURPOSE: :

The purpose of this bill is to direct the Public Service Commission to
establish a self-direct program for its industrial, commercial and
large users, in order to stimulate the growth and adoption of more
efficient use of energy, greater use of advanced energy management
products, deeper penetration of renewable energy resources such as
wind, solar, geothermal, and anaerobic digestion, wider deployment of
"distributed" energy resources, such as micro grids, roof-top solar,
fuel cells and other on-site power supplies, and storage.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS: :

Section 1 of the bill directs the Commission to commence a proceeding
to establish a self-direct program for its industrial, commercial and
large users, in order to stimulate the growth and adoption of more
efficient use of energy, greater use of advanced energy management
products, deeper penetration of renewable energy resources such as
wind, solar, geothermal, and anaerobic digestion, wider deployment of
"distributed" energy resources, such as micro grids, roof-top solar,
fuel cells and other on-site power supplies, and storage.

The bill establishes that the Commission, in collaboration with the
utilities and large industrial customers, shall develop, oversee and
issue guidelines that establish rules and principles for the
self-direct program, which shall include the following elements:

*Include a mechanism to recoup paid funds from self-direct customers
if it is determined that funds contained in the Energy Savings Account
were utilized erroneously or if planned energy efficiency savings did
not actually occur.

*After seven years make any unused surcharges contained in the Energy
Saving Account available for surcharges original purposes

*A method to measure and verify all claimed energy objectives, using
the same standards for data collection as other existing and future
clean energy surcharges.

*A requirement that a customer implementing a self-directed energy
optimization plan provide every two years, a brief report documenting
the measures taken to meet the goals of the self directed program.
The bill also would require the Commission to provide a report on the
Clean Energy Technology Program.

Section 2 provides for an immediate effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION: :

New York's energy policy increasingly recognizing the value of energy
efficiency. The State has dedicated significant amounts of ratepayer
collections and other assessments to increasing the adoption of energy
efficiency measures.

Large energy users, such as industrial facilities and institutional
campuses, have a very significant interest to invest in energy
efficiency. Such investments lower their operating costs and utility
bills and stabilize their future rates.


Some of the most cost-effective efficiency programs are those designed
for large energy users.{1) The industrial sector saves more energy per
program dollar than any other customer class but only a fraction of
their industrial energy efficiency potential is addressed through
current programs. Often large energy customers, due to their unique
needs, do not meet the demands, requirements or parameters for the
State-established programs.

This legislation will have significant positive benefits because
eligible large customers still contribute funding toward energy
efficiency programming but they may then direct those funds toward the
design, implementation and verification of energy-saving projects in
their own facilities. This legislation will provide more customer
control because traditional program offerings do not often meet their
needs or disproportionately benefit other rate classes.

All 50 states implement ratepayer-funded energy programs. Sixteen
states currently offer a self-direct provision for large customers.
Twelve other states allow some or all large customers to completely
opt out of paying for the energy efficiency resource.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: :

2016 - S. 7840 Passed Senate/A. 10716 - Rules Committee.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: :

The bill would have no impact on the State budget.

 EFFECTIVE DATE: :

Immediate.

(1) A.Chittum and S.Nowak, Money Well Spent: 2010 Industrial Energy
Efficiency Program Spending (Washington, DC: ACEEE, 2012).
